newsitem.title: USA: Orlando Utilities sees Fla. power unit back Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Orlando Utilities sees Fla. power unit back Thurs.

text.p: Orlando Utilities said Thursday that its Indian River 3 power unit near Titusville, Fla., will likely be available for full service later today or Friday.
"It's an intermediate unit. It will be available dependent on demand," a company spokesman said.
The unit, which can be fueled by natural gas or fuel oil, has been operating at 50 percent power since autumn.
Maximum generating capacity of the unit is 355 megawatts, but it usually generates about 324 megawatts during the winter, he said.
The Indian River plant, including two other dual-fired units, has a generating capacity of about 619 megawatts.

Temperatures in Florida are expected to average eight to 18 degrees Fahrenheit below normal this weekend and into early next week, with daytime lows in the Orlando area expected to be in the 30s and highs in the 50s.
